page: Microsoft Azure D96nlds_v6 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with 96 dedicated Intel vCPUs and 192 GB of total system RAM, corresponding to an exact allocation of 2 GB of memory per core. This low memory-to-core ratio focuses compute capacity on parallel processing tasks that do not demand extensive RAM capacity per thread. The server contains no discrete GPU accelerators, orienting its execution capabilities entirely around CPU processing.

A notable hardware characteristic of the D96nlds_v6 is its integrated 5669 GB NVMe SSD local storage. This large local storage volume affords low latency and high read and write performance for temporary scratch files, local caching tiers, or transient data structures without relying exclusively on remote attached volumes. From a cost-efficiency perspective, reducing the RAM allocation relative to the 96 vCPUs lowers infrastructure expense compared to standard balanced profiles, optimizing operational expenses for CPU-dominated pipelines.

The primary trade-off of the D96nlds_v6 lies in its constrained memory footprint relative to its extensive core density, which makes it unsuitable for expansive in-memory databases or memory-bound analytics frameworks. Instead, the hardware composition is appropriate for distributed compile jobs, CI/CD runners, parallel batch processing, ETL transformations, and network-demanding web services requiring immediate access to fast, high-capacity local scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D96nlds_v6 is a specialized compute-dense instance within the Dnldv6 series, architected for processing tasks requiring high core counts alongside fast local storage. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor and managed through Microsoft Hyper-V, the virtual machine provides 96 dedicated vCPUs and 192 GB of system memory, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU allocation. A key differentiator is the inclusion of 5669 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, enabling rapid scratch space and high-throughput temporary data persistence. The instance does not bundle GPU accelerators and is designed for workloads where massive parallel CPU throughput and local disk speeds take precedence over large RAM capacity. Qualitative cost efficiency is realized through the lower memory footprint per core, which minimizes memory overhead costs for CPU-dominated operations. Recommended workloads include distributed build systems, large-scale batch computation, extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, and fast-caching databases requiring direct local NVMe access.
